subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The radius of an air bubble is increasing at the rate of 1/2 cm/sec. At what rate is the volume of the bubble increasing when the radius is 1 cm?

mark_split.label: Differentiate V = (4/3)πr³ with respect to t

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate V = (4/3)πr³ with respect to t
steps.margin_note: First mark. An air bubble is a sphere, so V = (4/3)πr³. Here dr/dt is the one that is given and dV/dt is the unknown — the opposite way round to the balloon question.
lines: An air bubble is a sphere, so let r be its radius at time t.
Given: dr/dt = 1/2 cm/sec.  Asked: dV/dt when r = 1 cm.
Differentiate both sides with respect to time t:

recall.must_convey: That the bubble is a sphere with V = (4/3)πr³, and differentiating with respect to t gives dV/dt = 4πr²(dr/dt).
accept: a bubble is a sphere so volume is four by three pi r cubed
differentiate with respect to time to get four pi r squared d r by d t
half a centimetre per second is d r by d t and d v by d t is asked
bubble ante sphere, volume formula rasi differentiate cheyyali
d v by d t equals four pi r squared into d r by d t
the three cancels the three in the denominator
heard_as: four by three pi r cubed

steps.why: This is the same relation dV/dt = 4πr²(dr/dt) as the balloon question, used in the opposite direction: there dr/dt was the unknown, here dV/dt is.
common_mistakes: Using the surface area 4πr² as the volume formula.
Differentiating r³ as r² without the factor 3, which loses the cancellation.
Treating 1/2 cm/sec as a volume rate.
steps.memory_tip: Differentiating the sphere's volume gives its surface area, 4πr² — write that one line and both the balloon question and this one are already half done.

steps.label: Substitute r = 1 and dr/dt = 1/2
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Here the unknown dV/dt is already alone on the left, so this is a direct substitution with no rearranging. Keep the answer as 2π and write cm³/sec.

recall.must_convey: That substituting r = 1 and dr/dt = 1/2 gives dV/dt = 2π cm³/sec.
accept: four pi into one into half is two pi
the volume increases at two pi cubic centimetres per second
substitute r equal to one and d r by d t equal to half
r equal to one substitute cheste two pi vasthundi
the answer is two pi centimetre cube per second
about six point two eight cubic centimetres per second

steps.why: dV/dt is already the subject of the equation, so no rearranging is needed. The unit is cm³/sec because a volume changing per second is a volume rate.
common_mistakes: Writing 4π as the answer by forgetting to multiply by 1/2.
Dividing by 1/2 instead of multiplying, which gives 8π.
Giving the unit as cm²/sec instead of cm³/sec.
steps.memory_tip: With r = 1 the r² factor is just 1, so the whole answer is 4π halved, which is 2π.
